alignments.note: Finite verb with its subject pronoun (rule 17), headed on the lexical verb.
Object suffix rendered by the object pronoun (rule 18).
Assimilated article supplied by MACULA (rule 12); the ASV writes *silver* anarthrously (rule 29).

Finite verb; the ASV reaches its bare object suffix through the supplied *for*, which belongs to the verb's unit (rule 44), and writes that same word again over the elliptical comparative — *as* ***for*** *hid treasures* is *as [thou searchest] for hid treasures* — so the second occurrence joins this one discontinuous unit under rule 25. The competing reading gives *as for* to the `כְּ` as one rendering, but the ASV writes no comparative *as for* elsewhere and the second *for* answers to the verb's valency, which is what licensed the first.
Object suffix rendered by the object pronoun (rule 18).
Comparative `כְּ` rendered *as*, exactly as s004; the *for* standing after it is the verb's repeated valency preposition (rule 25) and not a second word for this morpheme.
Assimilated article with no written *the* (rules 12 and 29); MACULA's gloss *hidden* on this token contradicts its morphology and is a display defect (rule 39).
`מַטְמֹן` rendered *hid treasures*; the head stays on *treasures*, which carries the lexeme (rule 31).

The competing reading is named in the verb's note.
The gloss distribution on s009/s010 is reversed in MACULA; the morphology (article + plural noun) is what was read (rule 39).
